title: Transplant status and rejection
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's transplant status or transplant complication only.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for heart transplant.

HPI: Pt is a 42-year-old male presenting for routine surveillance following a heart transplant performed 6 years ago. Pt reports feeling well overall. Denies any symptoms of rejection, chest pain, shortness of breath, or palpitations. He remains stable on his current immunosuppression regimen. Compliance with tacrolimus is excellent. No new concerns voiced today.

Medication List:
- Tacrolimus 1mg BID
- Amlodipine 5mg daily
- Lisinopril 10mg daily

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Denies fever, chills, fatigue.
Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain, syncope.
Respiratory: Denies cough, SOB.
GI: Denies nausea, diarrhea.
Musculoskeletal: Denies joint pain.
Neuro: Denies headaches, dizziness.

Social History: Works full-time as a software engineer. Non-smoker. Occasional alcohol use. Lives with spouse and two children.

Family History: Father had hypertension. Mother had type 2 diabetes. No history of autoimmune disease.

Recent Labs:
- Tacrolimus level: 8.0 ng/mL (target range)
- Cr: 1.1 mg/dL
- K+: 4.2 mEq/L
- WBC: 6.5 x10^3/uL
- HbA1c: 5.7%

Vitals:
BP: 122/78 mmHg
HR: 72 bpm, RRR
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 98% on RA
Height: 5'10"
Weight: 185 lbs

Exam:
General: Alert and oriented x3. In no acute distress.
CV: Regular rhythm, no murmurs, S1/S2 heard. No peripheral edema.
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally. No wheezing or rales.
Abd: Soft, non-tender, non-distended.
Skin: No rashes or lesions noted.

Assessment:
1. Status post heart transplant. Pt is doing well on tacrolimus. No signs of rejection or other transplant complication.

Plan:
- Continue current tacrolimus and antihypertensive medications.
- Continue routine monitoring of tacrolimus trough levels.
- Follow up in 3 months for repeat labs and clinic visit.

Electronically signed,
L. Moreau, DO
